words.definition: verb: to object or show reluctance
words.example: Wallace disliked the cold, so he demurred when his friends suggested they go skiing in the Alps.

words.definition: adjective: not spending much money (but spending wisely)
words.example: Monte was no miser, but was simply frugal, wisely spending the little that he earned.

words.definition: adjective: being disrespectful; improperly forward or bold
words.example: Dexter, distraught over losing his pet dachshund, Madeline, found the police officer's questions impertinent -after all, he thought, did she have to pry into such details as to what Madeline's favorite snack was?

words.definition: noun: a mixture of multiple things
words.example: The band's music was an amalgam of hip-hop, flamenco and jazz, blending the three styles with surprising results.

words.definition: adjective: to be likely to socialize with others
words.example: Often we think that great leaders are those who are gregarious, always in the middle of a large group of people; yet, as Mahatma Gandhi and many others have shown us, leaders can also be introverted.

words.definition: noun: the condition of being susceptible to bribes or corruption
words.example: Even some of the most sacred sporting events are not immune to venality, as many of the officials have received substantial bribes to make biased calls.

words.definition: verb: to reproach; to scold
words.example: Bob took a risk walking into the "Students Barbershop"—in the end he had to upbraid the apparently drunk barber for giving him an uneven bowl cut.

words.definition: adjective: restless

words.example: The composer Wagner, while living on a limited salary, was so profligate as to line all the walls of his apartment with pure silk. Most lottery winners go from being conservative, frugal types to outright profligates who blow millions on fast cars, lavish homes, and giant yachts.

words.definition: noun: a long pompous speech; a tirade; verb: to deliver a long pompous speech or tirade

Tired of his parents haranguing him about his laziness and lack of initiative, Tyler finally moved out of home at the age of thirty-five.

words.definition: adjective: shapeless

words.definition: verb: to respect deeply

words.definition: adjective: open to more than one interpretation
words.example: The coach told his team, "Move towards that side of the field"; because he did not point, his directions were ambiguous, and the team had no idea to which side he was referring.

words.definition: adjective: (of a person) prone to unexpected and unpredictable changes in mood

words.definition: adjective: complicated, and difficult to comprehend
words.example: The physics lecture became so involved that the undergraduate's eyes glazed over.

words.definition: noun: bitterness and ill will
words.example: The acrimony between the president and vice-president sent a clear signal to voters: the health of the current administration was imperiled.

words.definition: adjective: standing out in a negative way; shockingly bad
words.example: The dictator's abuse of human rights was so egregious that many world leaders demanded that he be tried in an international court for genocide.

words.definition: noun: somebody who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions

words.definition: adjective: harmless and doesn't produce any ill effects

words.definition: adjective: still in existence (usually refers to documents).

words.definition: verb: to give a false representation to; misrepresent

words.definition: verb: to suggest something subtly

words.definition: adjective: exhibiting artistic skill; adjective: clever in a cunning way

words.definition: adjective: narrowly restricted in scope or outlook

words.definition: verb: to express strong disapproval

words.definition: noun: making of a false statement meant to injure a person's reputation

words.definition: verb: to reveal or make known something, usually unintentionally

words.definition: adjective: lacking

words.definition: adjective: (describes a person, speech, or style of writing) using very few words

words.definition: verb: to make less severe; to limit (a statement)

words.definition: adjective: to be in proportion or corresponding in degree or amount

words.definition: adjective: mixed or conflicting emotions about something

words.definition: adjective: unbiased; neutral

words.definition: adjective: truthful

words.definition: adjective: easily persuaded

words.definition: adjective: extremely frugal; miserly

words.definition: adjective: not normal

words.definition: noun: a deviation from what is normal or expected

words.definition: verb: to excite or inspire (someone) to action

words.definition: verb: to speak in an evasive way

words.definition: adjective: rashly or wastefully extravagant

words.definition: adjective: favorable, the opposite of sinister

words.definition: verb: to sap energy from

words.definition: verb: to reprimand harshly

words.definition: adjective: to be naïve and innocent

words.definition: verb: to assert

words.definition: adjective: overly sentimental to the point that it is disgusting

words.definition: adjective: marked by a lack of interest

words.definition: adjective: characteristic of rural life; awkwardly simple and provincial

words.definition: adjective: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse

words.definition: verb: avoid and stay away from deliberately; stay clear of

words.definition: adjective: having or demonstrating ability to recognize or draw fine distinctions

words.definition: adjective: relating to the pleasant aspects of the country

words.definition: noun: the quality of talking or writing easily and continuously

words.definition: adjective: occurring by happy chance; having no cause or apparent cause

words.definition: adjective: showing respect

words.definition: adjective: showing modest reserve; lacking self-confidence
words.example: As a young girl she was diffident and reserved, but now as an adult, she is confident and assertive.

words.definition: noun: a strong liking

words.definition: adjective: disinclined to talk, not revealing one's thoughts

words.definition: adjective: characterized by good taste in manners and conduct

words.definition: verb: criticize severely or angrily

words.definition: verb: reach the highest or most decisive point

words.definition: adjective: fixed firmly or securely

words.definition: noun: the power to foresee the future

words.definition: adjective: expecting unquestioning obedience; characteristic of an absolute ruler

words.definition: adjective: not serious in content or attitude or behavior

words.definition: verb: keep from happening or arising; make impossible

words.definition: verb: to chuckle, laugh merrily, often in a breathy, muffled way

words.definition: adjective: improperly forward or bold

words.definition: noun: inactivity resulting from lethargy and lack of vigor or energy

words.definition: adjective: conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry

words.definition: adjective: characterized by unusual lightness and delicacy

words.definition: adjective: impossible to stop or prevent

words.definition: adjective: marked by extreme care in treatment of details

words.definition: adjective: highly opinionated, not accepting that one's own beliefs may not be correct

words.definition: adjective: instructive (especially excessively)

words.definition: noun: one who professes great sensitivity to the beauty of art and nature

words.definition: adjective: mysterious or vague, usually intentionally

words.definition: adjective: marked by extreme intensity of emotions or convictions

words.definition: adjective: free of deceit

words.definition: adjective: characteristic of one eager to fight

words.definition: noun: a situation that seems impossible because it is made of opposite things
words.example: When he first arrived in the desert, Alex did not believe the paradox that drinking hot tea could make a person feel cool.

words.definition: adjective: only slightly related to the main point
words.example: The professor's tangential remarks about the history of the printing press were interesting, but they did not directly relate to the main topic of our discussion on modern technology.

words.definition: noun: harsh criticism or public disgrace
words.example: Due to the scandal, the politician faced intense public opprobrium, with harsh criticism and condemnation filling the media, as citizens expressed their outrage and disappointment over the ethical breach.

words.definition: adjective: burdensome; difficult to bear
words.example: The task proved onerous, requiring a lot of effort. Despite the difficulty, completing it successfully brought immense satisfaction. I found the project's demands challenging, but the reward made the hard work worthwhile.

words.definition: noun: truthfulness and accuracy
words.example: Due to the high degree of truthfulness, the detective found it easy to find the criminal, because the witness gave veracity to the court.

words.definition: adjective: high‑sounding but with little meaning; inflated
words.example: The bombastic speaker used exaggerated language, making grand pronouncements that seemed designed more to impress the audience than to communicate actual information or substance.

words.definition: verb: to strip or rid of property or rights
words.example: I will divest my shares of the company because the business has had a rough year. Their profits went down, and I don't want to risk any more money on it.

words.definition: adjective: willing to obey rules or requests
words.example: The store's new policy made many customers compliant, but some still found ways to bend the rules.

words.definition: adjective: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably
words.example: The volatile nature of the market made investors nervous, as they worried about the possibility of sudden and unpredictable changes. It caused them to re-evaluate their investments.

words.definition: adjective: strongly supporting one side
words.example: The biased group's actions were viewed as partisan, favoring their own members over others. This led to intense disagreements, as some felt the decisions were unfair to those who didn't belong.

words.definition: adjective: implied though not directly stated
words.example: The subtle clues in her expression gave an implicit understanding of the situation, and everyone knew without needing an explanation or words, that something was not right, it was obvious to all.

words.definition: noun: conformity to accepted standards; correctness
words.example: She always behaved with propriety, never gossiping or causing any trouble, because she knew that her reputation was important for her career, and she wanted to be seen as professional.

words.definition: adjective: just coming into existence; beginning to develop
words.example: Because of the nascent technology, the company needed more time to fully develop its product to meet the demands of its consumers.

words.definition: verb: to disagree with authority
words.example: Amidst the heated debate, a wave of dissent surged, with many people openly disagreeing with the proposed changes, their voices echoing with disapproval and a determination to protect their beliefs.

words.definition: adjective: very weak or slight
words.example: The fragile bridge, its structure tenuous, swayed precariously in the wind, and the hikers worried about the integrity of its supports, as they were uncertain whether it would hold.

words.definition: verb: to become less intense or widespread
words.example: The rain began to abate as the storm moved eastward, allowing the sun to peek through the clouds and illuminate the colorful flowers in the garden, bringing joy

words.definition: noun: use of trickery to achieve a purpose
words.example: Due to the politician's chicanery, the public lost faith in the government. The lies and deception led many citizens to doubt the intentions and honesty of their leaders.

words.definition: adjective: not important or significant
words.example: The movie's plot was inconsequential to the overall themes, as the director focused on the visuals and atmosphere rather than a deep, meaningful story, and the audience was left confused.

words.definition: noun: craftiness
words.example: Little Timmy was full of guile, often telling his mommy someone was at the door--then, when her back was turned, he would raid the chocolate stash.

words.definition: noun: something that discourages action
words.example: The police presence served as a deterrent, making potential criminals reconsider their actions. They knew the risks of getting caught were high with officers nearby, discouraging any illegal behavior.

words.definition: adjective: cautious, not trusting
words.example: Years of being stuck in the loud and crowded shelter made the dog wary of other animals.

words.definition: noun: a speech praising someone who has died
words.example: The touching eulogy, filled with heartfelt memories and anecdotes, painted a vivid picture of the person's life, celebrating their kindness and the impact they had on others, leaving everyone deeply moved.

words.definition: noun: keen insight and quick judgment
words.example: Her business acumen was evident when she turned a small, struggling company into a profitable enterprise within just two years, demonstrating a keen understanding of the market and strategic decision-making.

words.definition: adjective: habitually reserved and uncommunicative
words.example: While the CEO enthusiastically shares his plans and agenda with all who will listen, the CFO is far more taciturn, rarely revealing his perspective.

words.definition: noun: an expert judge in matters of taste
words.example: The restaurant critic, a true connoisseur, savored the exquisite flavors of the dish. His discerning palate detected a hint of truffle, a whisper of citrus, and the perfect balance.

words.definition: adjective: intensely passionate
words.example: The ardent speeches from the politician were always filled with fervid language, captivating the audience with passionate calls to action, even though some felt the promises were exaggerated.

words.definition: adjective: careful to consider all circumstances; cautious
words.example: The detective, a circumspect individual, approached the crime scene cautiously, carefully examining every detail. His goal was to solve the case, understanding all clues.

words.definition: noun: a loud and continuous noise
words.example: The loud clamor of the crowd was almost unbearable, as everyone was screaming and shouting, hoping to get the attention of the performers who were on the stage.

words.definition: adjective: more than is needed; very fancy
words.example: Fido's birthday feast was lavish; most guests thought that a dog would not be able to appreciate the bits of gold in his steak-flavored ice cream.

words.definition: verb: to state or assert confidently
words.example: As he began to aver his point, the speaker realized that some audience members were losing interest. It became apparent that he needed to explain the situation, and the crowd began to listen.

words.definition: verb: to make easier
words.example: Classical music, unlike many types of music, will generally facilitate learning and improve memory.

words.definition: adjective: of the same or similar kind
words.example: The scientific study was homogeneous, with all participants sharing similar backgrounds, which unfortunately limited the diversity of perspectives and viewpoints within the research findings.

words.definition: adjective: able to express ideas clearly and effectively
words.example: He found it difficult to articulate his thoughts during the meeting because he was nervous, but he knew the importance of communicating effectively with his colleagues.

decks.name: Common Words - Fill in the Blank I

words.definition: verb: to object or show reluctance
words.example: Wallace disliked the cold, so he demurred when his friends suggested they go skiing in the Alps.

words.definition: adjective: not spending much money (but spending wisely)
words.example: Monte was no miser, but was simply frugal, wisely spending the little that he earned.

words.definition: adjective: being disrespectful; improperly forward or bold
words.example: Dexter, distraught over losing his pet dachshund, Madeline, found the police officer's questions impertinent -after all, he thought, did she have to pry into such details as to what Madeline's favorite snack was?

words.definition: noun: a mixture of multiple things
words.example: The band's music was an amalgam of hip-hop, flamenco and jazz, blending the three styles with surprising results.

words.definition: adjective: to be likely to socialize with others
words.example: Often we think that great leaders are those who are gregarious, always in the middle of a large group of people; yet, as Mahatma Gandhi and many others have shown us, leaders can also be introverted.

words.definition: noun: the condition of being susceptible to bribes or corruption
words.example: Even some of the most sacred sporting events are not immune to venality, as many of the officials have received substantial bribes to make biased calls.

words.definition: verb: to reproach; to scold
words.example: Bob took a risk walking into the "Students Barbershop"—in the end he had to upbraid the apparently drunk barber for giving him an uneven bowl cut.

words.definition: adjective: restless
words.example: The crowd grew restive as the comedian's opening jokes fell flat.

words.definition: adjective: spending resources recklessly or wastefully; noun: someone who spends resources recklessly or wastefully
words.example: The composer Wagner, while living on a limited salary, was so profligate as to line all the walls of his apartment with pure silk. Most lottery winners go from being conservative, frugal types to outright profligates who blow millions on fast cars, lavish homes, and giant yachts.

words.definition: noun: a long pompous speech; a tirade; verb: to deliver a long pompous speech or tirade
words.example: Dinner at Billy's was more a punishment than a reward, since anyone who sat at the dinner table would have to listen to Billy's father's interminable harangues against the government. Tired of his parents haranguing him about his laziness and lack of initiative, Tyler finally moved out of home at the age of thirty-five.

words.definition: adjective: shapeless
words.example: His study plan for the GRE was at best amorphous; he would do questions from random pages in any one of seven test prep books.

words.definition: verb: to respect deeply
words.example: The professor, despite his sleep-inducing lectures, was venerated amongst his colleagues, publishing more papers yearly than all of his peers combined.

words.definition: adjective: open to more than one interpretation
words.example: The coach told his team, "Move towards that side of the field"; because he did not point, his directions were ambiguous, and the team had no idea to which side he was referring.

words.definition: adjective: (of a person) prone to unexpected and unpredictable changes in mood
words.example: The fact that Ella's moods were as mercurial as the weather was problematic for her relationships—it didn't help that she lived in Chicago.

words.definition: adjective: complicated, and difficult to comprehend
words.example: The physics lecture became so involved that the undergraduate's eyes glazed over.

words.definition: noun: bitterness and ill will
words.example: The acrimony between the president and vice-president sent a clear signal to voters: the health of the current administration was imperiled.

words.definition: adjective: standing out in a negative way; shockingly bad
words.example: The dictator's abuse of human rights was so egregious that many world leaders demanded that he be tried in an international court for genocide.

words.definition: noun: somebody who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions
words.example: Lady Gaga, in challenging what it means to be clothed, is an iconoclast for wearing a "meat dress" to a prominent awards show.

words.definition: adjective: harmless and doesn't produce any ill effects
words.example: Everyone found Nancy's banter innocuous—except for Mike, who felt like she was intentionally picking on him.

words.definition: adjective: still in existence (usually refers to documents).
words.example: Despite many bookstores closing, experts predict that some form of book dealing will still be extant generations from now.

words.definition: verb: to give a false representation to; misrepresent
words.example: The smile on her face belies the pain she must feel after the death of her husband.

words.definition: verb: to suggest something subtly
words.example: At first Manfred's teachers intimated to his parents that he was not suited to skip a grade; when his parents protested, teachers explicitly told them that, notwithstanding the boy's precocity, he was simply too immature to jump to the 6th grade.

words.definition: adjective: exhibiting artistic skill; adjective: clever in a cunning way
words.example: Picasso is generally considered the most artful member of the Cubist movement. Bernie Madoff's artful Ponzi scheme stole billions of dollars from investors and is considered the largest financial fraud in U.S. history.

words.definition: adjective: narrowly restricted in scope or outlook
words.example: Jasmine was sad to admit it, but her fledgling relationship with Jacob did not work out because his culinary tastes were simply too parochial; "After all," she quipped on her blog, "he considered Chef Boyardee ethnic food."

words.definition: verb: to express strong disapproval
words.example: After being caught in bed with a mistress, the mayor was quickly censured by the city council.

words.definition: noun: making of a false statement meant to injure a person's reputation
words.example: With the presidential primaries well under way, the air is thick with calumny, and the mud already waist-high.

words.definition: verb: to reveal or make known something, usually unintentionally
words.example: With the gold medal at stake, the gymnast awaited his turn, his quivering lip betraying his intense emotions.

words.definition: adjective: lacking
words.example: She did not think her vocabulary was wanting, yet there were so many words that inevitably she found a few she didn't know.

words.definition: adjective: (describes a person, speech, or style of writing) using very few words
words.example: While Martha always swooned over the hunky, laconic types in romantic comedies, her boyfriends inevitably were very talkative—and not very hunky.

words.definition: verb: to make less severe; to limit (a statement)
words.example: Chris qualified his love for San Francisco, adding he didn't like the weather there as much as he liked the weather in Los Angeles.

words.definition: adjective: to be in proportion or corresponding in degree or amount
words.example: The convicted felon's life sentence was commensurate with the heinousness of his crime.

words.definition: adjective: mixed or conflicting emotions about something
words.example: Sam was ambivalent about studying for the exam because doing so ate up a lot of his time, yet he was able to improve his analytical skills.

words.definition: adjective: unbiased; neutral
words.example: The potential juror knew the defendant, and therefore could not serve on the jury, which must consist only of disinterested members.

words.definition: verb: to weaken (usually paired with an abstract term)
words.example: The student undermined the teacher's authority by questioning the teacher's judgment on numerous occasions.

words.definition: adjective: truthful
words.example: While we elect our leaders in the hope that every word they speak will be veracious, history has shown that such a hope is naive.

words.definition: adjective: easily persuaded
words.example: Even though she did not like the outdoors, Shirley was generally amenable and so her brother was able to persuade her to go camping.

words.definition: adjective: extremely frugal; miserly
words.example: Katie is so parsimonious that she only buys a pair of socks if all of her other socks have holes in them.

words.definition: adjective: not normal
words.example: According to those who do not believe in climate change, the extreme weather over the last five years is simply anomalous—daily temperatures should return to their old averages, they believe.

words.definition: noun: a deviation from what is normal or expected
words.example: Aberrations in climate have become the norm: rarely a week goes by without some meteorological phenomenon making headlines.

words.definition: verb: to excite or inspire (someone) to action
words.example: At mile 23 of his first marathon, Kyle had all but given up, until he noticed his friends and family holding a banner that read, "Go Kyle"; galvanized, he broke into a gallop, finishing the last three miles in less than 20 minutes.

words.definition: adjective: confusing or ambiguous
words.example: The findings of the study were equivocal—the two researchers had different opinions on what the results signified.

words.definition: verb: to clear of accusation, blame, suspicion, or doubt with supporting arguments or proof
words.example: Even seven Tour de France wins cannot vindicate Lance Armstrong in the eyes of the public--that the athlete used performance enhancing drugs invalidates all those wins.

words.definition: verb: to reprimand harshly
words.example: Though chastised for eating the snacks for the party, Lawrence shrugged off his mother's harsh words, and continued to plow through jars of cookies and boxes of donuts.

words.definition: verb: to speak in an evasive way
words.example: The cynic quipped, "There is not much variance in politicians; they all seem to prevaricate".

words.definition: adjective: rashly or wastefully extravagant
words.example: Successful professional athletes who do not fall prey to prodigality seem to be the exception—most live decadent lives.

words.definition: adjective: favorable, the opposite of sinister
words.example: Despite an auspicious beginning, Mike's road trip became a series of mishaps, and he was soon stranded and penniless, leaning against his wrecked automobile.

words.definition: verb: to sap energy from
words.example: John preferred to avoid equatorial countries; the intense sun would always leave him enervated after he'd spent the day sightseeing.

words.definition: verb: to reprimand harshly
words.example: Drill sergeants are known to castigate new recruits so mercilessly that the latter often break down during their first week in training.

words.definition: adjective: to be naïve and innocent
words.example: Two-years in Manhattan had changed Jenna from an ingenuous girl from the suburbs to a jaded urbanite, unlikely to fall for any ruse, regardless of how elaborate.

words.definition: verb: to assert
words.example: The scientist maintained that the extinction of dinosaurs was most likely brought about by a drastic change in climate.

decks.name: Common Words - Fill in the Blank II

words.definition: adjective: overly sentimental to the point that it is disgusting
words.example: The film was incredibly mawkish, introducing highly likeable characters only to have them succumb to a devastating illness by the end of the movie.

words.definition: adjective: marked by a lack of interest
words.example: Mr. Thompson was so talented at teaching math that even normally apathetic students took interest.

words.definition: noun: a trite or obvious remark
words.example: The professor argued that many statements regarded as wise in previous times, such as the Golden Rule, are now regarded as mere platitudes.

words.definition: adjective: characteristic of rural life; awkwardly simple and provincial
words.example: The vacation cabin had no electricity and no indoor plumbing, but despite these inconveniences, Nigel adored its rustic charm.

words.definition: adjective: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
words.example: The professor used such banal expression that many students in the class either fell asleep from boredom or stayed awake to complete his sentences and humor friends.

words.definition: verb: avoid and stay away from deliberately; stay clear of
words.example: Politicians are the masters of eschewing morals; academics are the masters of eschewing clarity.

words.definition: adjective: having or demonstrating ability to recognize or draw fine distinctions
words.example: The lawyer had an incisive mind, able in a flash to dissect a hopelessly tangled issue and isolate the essential laws at play.

words.definition: verb: make worse
words.example: Her sleeplessness exacerbated her cold--when she woke up the next day, her sinuses were completely blocked.

words.definition: adjective: relating to the pleasant aspects of the country
words.example: The noble families of England once owned vast expanses of beautiful, bucolic land.

words.definition: adjective: relevant and appropriate
words.example: The professor wanted to tell the jury in detail about his new book, but the lawyer said it wasn't germane to the charges in the cases.

words.definition: noun: the quality of talking or writing easily and continuously
words.example: The professor's volubility knows no bounds; he could talk through a hurricane and elaborate a point from one St. Patrick's Day to the next.

words.definition: adjective: occurring by happy chance; having no cause or apparent cause
words.example: Missing my train turned out to be quite fortuitous since I ran into a childhood friend on the next train and we were able to reconnect after so many years.

words.definition: verb: make unclear; adjective: known by only a few
words.example: On the Smith's drive through the Grand Canyon, Mr. Smith's big head obscured much of Mrs. Robinson's view, so that she only saw momentary patches of red rock. Many of the biggest movie stars were once obscure actors who got only bit roles in long forgotten films.

words.definition: adjective: showing respect
words.example: If you ever have the chance to meet the president, stand up straight and be deferential.

words.definition: verb: deny or contradict; speak against or oppose
words.example: I can't gainsay a single piece of evidence James has presented, but I still don't trust his conclusion.

words.definition: adjective: difficult to penetrate; incomprehensible to one of ordinary understanding or knowledge
words.example: I found Ulysses recondite and never finished the book, waiting instead to read it with someone else so we could penetrate its meaning together.

words.definition: adjective: showing modest reserve; lacking self-confidence
words.example: As a young girl she was diffident and reserved, but now as an adult, she is confident and assertive.

words.definition: adjective: concerned with the appreciation of beauty; noun: a set of principles underlying and guiding the work of a particular artist or artistic movement.
words.example: The director, not known for his aesthetic sensibilities, decided not to use costumes at all, and put on the play in everyday clothing. The artist operated according to a peculiar aesthetic, not considering any photograph to be worth publishing unless it contained a marine mammal.

words.definition: noun: an excessive supply; verb: supply with an excess of
words.example: The Internet offers such a glut of news related stories that many find it difficult to know which story to read first. In the middle of economic crises, hiring managers find their inboxes glutted with resumes.

words.definition: noun: a strong liking
words.example: Monte had a predilection for the fine things in life: Cuban cigars, 200 dollar bottles of wine, and trips to the French Riviera.

words.definition: adjective: willing to be bold in social situations or to take risks
words.example: As all of the other campers cowered in their tents, Bill, armed only with a flashlight, audaciously tracked down the bear that had raided their food.

words.definition: adjective: without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious
words.example: Among the tall trees and flower fields, the building seemed out of place with its conspicuous, cold concrete and angular steel exterior.

words.definition: adjective: disinclined to talk, not revealing one's thoughts
words.example: When asked about her father, Helen lost her outward enthusiasm and became rather reticent.

words.definition: adjective: characterized by good taste in manners and conduct
words.example: Sally's parties are decorous affairs, and instead of the usual beer and music, there is tea and intellectual conversation.

words.definition: verb: acknowledge defeat; verb: admit (to a wrongdoing); verb: give over; surrender or relinquish to the physical control of another
words.example: I concede. You win! After a long, stern lecture from her father, Olivia conceded to having broken the window. The Spanish were forced to concede much of the territory they had previously conquered.

words.definition: verb: criticize severely or angrily
words.example: Showing no patience, the manager utterly lambasted the sales team that lost the big account.

words.definition: verb: reach the highest or most decisive point
words.example: Beethoven's musical genius culminated in the 9th Symphony, which many consider his greatest work.

words.definition: adjective: fixed firmly or securely
words.example: By the time we reach 60-years old, most of our habits are so entrenched that it is difficult for us to change.

words.definition: noun: the power to foresee the future
words.example: Baxter's warnings about investing in technology stocks seemed like an act of prescience after the whole market declined significantly.

words.definition: adjective: serving no useful purpose; adjective: more than is needed, desired, or required
words.example: How can we hope to stay open if we don't eliminate all superfluous spending, like catered meetings and free acupuncture Tuesday? The third paragraph in your essay is superfluous and can be deleted.

words.definition: noun: the trait of being rude and impertinent; noun: feeling of deep and bitter anger and ill-will; verb: to strongly bother, vex, annoy, exasperate
words.example: The speeding car had the gall to switch five lanes at once, run through a red light, and then cut off a police car before finally coming to a stop in front of a sea of flashing red lights. In an act of gall, Leah sent compromising photos of her ex-boyfriend to all his co-workers and professional contacts. I try to look for the best in Gwendolyn, but her bad attitude really galls me.

words.definition: adjective: expecting unquestioning obedience; characteristic of an absolute ruler
words.example: The coach was dictatorial in his approach: no players could ever argue or question his approach.

words.definition: adjective: habitually complaining
words.example: The querulous old woman was beginning to wear down even the happier members of the staff with her ceaseless complaining.

words.definition: adjective: not serious in content or attitude or behavior
words.example: Compared to Juliet's passionate concern for human rights, Jake's non-stop concern about football seems somewhat frivolous.

words.definition: verb: keep from happening or arising; make impossible
words.example: The manager specified that all other gates be locked, to preclude the possibility of persons without tickets entering the arena undetected.

words.definition: verb: to chuckle, laugh merrily, often in a breathy, muffled way
words.example: Walking into the cafe, I could hear happy, chortling people and smell the rich aroma of roasted coffee beans.

words.definition: adjective: improperly forward or bold
words.example: In an impudent move, the defendant spoke out of order to say terribly insulting things to the judge.

words.definition: noun: inactivity resulting from lethargy and lack of vigor or energy
words.example: After work, I was expecting my colleagues to be enthusiastic about the outing, but I found them in a state of complete torpor.

words.definition: adjective: conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry
words.example: In giving Marcia a particular vociferous response, Paul caused people at every other table in the restaurant to turn around and look at them angrily.

words.definition: adjective: characterized by unusual lightness and delicacy
words.example: The gossamer wings of a butterfly, which allow it to fly, are also a curse, so delicate that they are often damaged.

words.definition: noun: an act of deliberate betrayal; a breach of a trust
words.example: Sure, he was the best salesman in the company; but Michael had abused the trust of the firm, sharing product secrets with a competitor, and for such perfidy he was terminated.

words.definition: adjective: impossible to stop or prevent
words.example: The rise of the computer was an inexorable shift in technology and culture.

words.definition: verb: make less severe or harsh; verb: lessen the severity of an offense
words.example: I can only spend so much time mitigating your disagreements with your wife, and at certain point, you need to do it on your own. If it weren't for the mitigating circumstances, he would have certainly lost his job.

words.definition: adjective: marked by extreme care in treatment of details
words.example: The Japanese noodle maker was meticulous in making his noodles and would never let another person take over the task.

words.definition: adjective: highly opinionated, not accepting that one's own beliefs may not be correct
words.example: Bryan is dogmatic in his belief that the earth is flat, claiming that all pictures of a spherical earth are computer generated.

words.definition: verb: give rise to
words.example: The restrictions of the Treaty of Versailles were so severe that they engendered deep hatred and resentment in the German people.

words.definition: adjective: instructive (especially excessively)
words.example: Tolstoy's The Death of Ivan Ilyich is a didactic novel, instructing the reader on how to live a good life.

words.definition: noun: one who professes great sensitivity to the beauty of art and nature
words.example: A true aesthete, Marty would spend hours at the Guggenheim Museum, staring at the same Picasso.

words.definition: adjective: mysterious or vague, usually intentionally
words.example: Since Sarah did not want her husband to guess the Christmas present she had bought him, she only answered cryptically when he would ask her questions about it.

words.definition: noun: a state of guilt
words.example: Since John had left his banana peel at the top of the stairwell, he accepted culpability for Martha's broken leg.

decks.name: Common Words - Fill in the Blank III

words.definition: adjective: discontented as toward authority
words.example: After watching his superior take rations from the soldiers, he quickly became disaffected and rebelled.

words.definition: adjective: standing above others in quality or position
words.example: Shakespeare is an eminent author in the English language, but I find his writing uninteresting and melodramatic.

words.definition: adjective: marked by extreme intensity of emotions or convictions
words.example: While the other employees responded to the bad news in a measured way, Andrew responded in a vehement manner, tipping over his desk and shouting at the top of his lungs.

words.definition: verb: cleverly find a way out of one's duties or obligations
words.example: One way of circumventing the GRE is to apply to a grad school that does not require GRE scores.

words.definition: adjective: stubbornly resistant to authority or control
words.example: Used to studious high school students, Martha was unprepared for the refractory Kindergarteners who neither sat still nor listened to a single word she said.

words.definition: verb: take the place or move into the position of
words.example: For many, a cell phone has supplanted a traditional phone; in fact, most 20-somethings don't even have a traditional phone anymore

words.definition: noun: distinctive and showy elegance
words.example: Jim, with his typical panache, came to the wedding reception with a top hat and cane.

words.definition: verb: place side by side for contrast
words.example: The appeal of her paintings comes from a classical style which is juxtaposed with modern themes.

words.definition: verb: come from; be connected by a relationship of blood, for example; verb: reason by deduction; establish by deduction
words.example: Many words in the English language are derived from Latin, including the word "derive." From the multiple set of footprints in the living room, the investigator derived an important clue: Sheila was not alone in the room at the time of the murder.

words.definition: verb: make something bad better
words.example: "Three Cups of Tea" tells the story of western man who hopes to ameliorate poverty and the lack of education in Afghanistan.

words.definition: adjective: admitting of no doubt or misunderstanding; having only one meaning or interpretation and leading to only one conclusion
words.example: The President's first statement on the subject was vague and open to competing interpretations, so when he spoke to Congress about the same subject later, he was careful to make his position completely unequivocal.

words.definition: verb: spread negative information about
words.example: Todd was noble after the divorce, choosing to say only complimentary things about Barbara, but Barbara did not hesitate to vilify Todd.

words.definition: verb: choose not to consume or take part in (particularly something enjoyable)
words.example: Considered a health nut, Jessica abstained from anything containing sugar--even chocolate.

words.definition: adjective: free of deceit
words.example: At first I thought my niece was guileless, but I then found myself buying her ice cream every time we passed a shop.

words.definition: verb: contain or include; verb: consider (an instance of something) as part of a general rule or principle
words.example: The rogue wave quickly subsumed the pier and boardwalk, destroying everything in its path. Don Quixote of La Mancha subsumes all other modern novels, demonstrating modern literary devices and predating even the idea of a postmodern, metanarrative.

words.definition: adjective: marked by or showing hopelessness
words.example: After her third pet dog died, Marcia was simply forlorn: this time even the possibility of buying a new dog no longer held any joy.

words.definition: adjective: characteristic of one eager to fight
words.example: Tom said that he was arguing the matter purely for philosophical reasons, but his belligerent tone indicated an underlying anger about the issue.

words.definition: adjective: not inclined towards physical exertion or effort; slow and relaxed
