words.example: After finding an anomaly in the data, she knew that she would have to conduct her experiment again.

words.definition: adjective: (used of conduct or character) deserving or bringing disgrace or shame
words.example: Since the politician preached ethics and morality, his texting of revealing photographs was ignominious, bringing shame on both himself and his party.

words.definition: noun: someone who exhibits great independence in thought and action
words.example: Officer Kelly was a maverick, rarely following police protocols or adopting the conventions for speech common among his fellow officers.

words.definition: adjective: expressing disapproval (usu. refers to a term)
words.example: Most psychologists object to the pejorative term "shrink", believing that they expand the human mind, not limit it.

words.definition: adjective: timid by nature or revealing fear and nervousness
words.example: Since this was her first time debating on stage and before an audience, Di's voice was timorous and quiet for the first 10 minutes.

words.definition: verb: support and strengthen
words.example: The case for the suspect's innocence was bolstered considerably by the fact that neither fingerprints nor DNA were found at the scene.

words.definition: adjective: full of or showing high-spirited merriment
words.example: The presidential candidate and her supporters were jovial once it was clear that she had won.

words.definition: adjective: lasting a very short time
words.example: The unpredictable and transient nature of deja vu makes it a very difficult phenomenon to study properly.

words.definition: noun: a trite or obvious remark
words.example: Herbert regarded the minister's remark as a mere banality until Sharon pointed out profound implications to the seemingly obvious words.

words.definition: verb: to express criticism towards
words.example: At first, Sarah was going to yell at the boy, but she didn't want to reproach him for telling the truth about the situation.

words.definition: adjective: wasting time
words.example: Lawyers use dilatory tactics so that it takes years before the case is actually decided.

words.definition: adjective: having or showing profound knowledge
words.example: Before the Internet, the library was typically where you would find erudite readers.

words.definition: noun: the feeling of remorse or guilt that comes from doing something bad
words.example: Those who show contrition during their prison terms--especially when under review by a parole board--often get shortened sentences.

words.definition: adjective: marked by quiet and caution and secrecy; taking pains to avoid being observed
words.example: While at work, George and his boss Regina felt the need to be as furtive as possible about their romantic relationship.

words.definition: verb: call forth (emotions, feelings, and responses)
words.example: Just smiling--even if you are depressed--can elicit feelings of pleasure and happiness.

words.definition: adjective: unaffected by strong emotion or prejudice
words.example: A good scientist should be dispassionate, focusing purely on what the evidence says, without personal attachment.

words.definition: noun: an intense feeling of dislike or aversion
words.example: Maria had an antipathy for tour groups, often bolting to the other side of the museum as soon as she saw a chaperone leading a group of wide-eyed tourists.

words.definition: noun: a state of uncertainty about what should be done (usually following some important event)
words.example: Ever since Elvira resigned as the head of marketing, everything about our sales strategy has been in a state of flux.

words.definition: adjective: avoiding waste, efficient
words.example: Journalists favor an economical style of writing, in which no unnecessary words are used and every sentence is as short as possible.

words.definition: adjective: demanding considerable mental effort and skill; testing powers of endurance
words.example: In order to deal with the arduous cross-country journey, truck drivers often survive on a string of caffeinated drinks, staying awake for up to 30 hours at a time.

words.definition: verb: reduce the length of something
words.example: The soccer game was truncated when the monsoon rain began to fall.

decks.name: Common Words - Fill in the Blank VII

words.definition: adjective: using more words than necessary
words.example: The lengthy speech of the verbose man at the town hall meeting, filled with unnecessary details and complex terminology, made it difficult for the audience to understand his main points, and many people were left feeling confused.

words.definition: adjective: not secret or hidden
words.example: The disagreement between the neighbors grew from quiet, angry looks to overt hatred as they began throwing eggs at each other's houses.

words.definition: adjective: fluent and persuasive
words.example: The lawyer's eloquent speech captivated the courtroom, as he skillfully presented his case, using persuasive language and clear arguments that resonated with the jury, leaving them thoroughly impressed.

words.definition: adjective: not exactly known, decided, or fixed
words.example: The investigation into the mysterious disappearance of the ancient artifact yielded a surprising result: the evidence remained indeterminate, leaving the investigators puzzled and uncertain about the truth.

words.definition: noun: official approval or praise
words.example: I was hoping for some kind of approbation after finishing the project, but it appears my boss doesn't care. He is always busy with other tasks.

words.definition: adjective: showing great energy or enthusiasm
words.example: The zealous student was excited to learn about new topics, but the teacher knew they needed to slow down and understand each subject before moving ahead.

words.definition: noun: the ability to produce the desired effect
words.example: The drug's efficacy in treating the illness was remarkable. Doctors observed the significant positive impact of the medication on patients, noting a swift reduction in the severity of symptoms and a general improvement in their condition.

words.definition: adjective: hard to manage or solve
words.example: The complex problem proved intractable for the team; they struggled to find a solution. Despite their efforts, the issue persisted, and other attempts failed.

words.definition: noun: large or excessive amount
words.example: With a plethora of options, the couple felt overwhelmed. They debated between a beach vacation, a mountain getaway, or a city adventure. Ultimately, they wanted something relaxing.

words.definition: adjective: very talkative
words.example: The student, usually loquacious, was unusually quiet during the exam. Perhaps the difficult questions and the pressure to perform well had caused them to lose their words.

words.definition: verb: to ease or lessen pain or trouble
words.example: To alleviate the pain in her leg, she took a pill. The medicine, which was supposed to help, didn't work very well. Now, she thinks that she may need to see a doctor.

words.definition: verb: to dry out completely
words.example: The farmer hoped the sun would dry the plants, but the weather was very humid. Sadly, the crops started to desiccate, so he quickly needed to find a solution to save his harvest.

words.definition: adjective: stated clearly and in detail
words.example: The instructions are explicit; I need to be direct and clear. I want to finish the work and get some ice cream. After this, I can watch a movie and relax before I go to bed tonight.

words.definition: adjective: secret or hidden
words.example: The attack was intended to be covert, but before it could begin, the entire plan was revealed to the target.

words.definition: noun: a perfect example of a quality or type
words.example: The movie was an epitome of the director's vision, showcasing his unique style and storytelling techniques through stunning visuals and a captivating narrative that enthralled audiences.

words.definition: adjective: easily deceived
words.example: Although he was very gullible, the old man was always happy to help his neighbors. His kindness made up for the fact that he was easily tricked by others.

words.definition: verb: to make something impure by adding inferior substances
words.example: The chef was careful to adulterate the recipe with a pinch of salt, as he knew the customers would taste a big difference in the flavor of the soup.

words.definition: noun: a situation that seems impossible because it is made of opposite things
words.example: When he first arrived in the desert, Alex did not believe the paradox that drinking hot tea could make a person feel cool.

words.definition: adjective: only slightly related to the main point
words.example: The professor's tangential remarks about the history of the printing press were interesting, but they did not directly relate to the main topic of our discussion on modern technology.

words.definition: noun: harsh criticism or public disgrace
words.example: Due to the scandal, the politician faced intense public opprobrium, with harsh criticism and condemnation filling the media, as citizens expressed their outrage and disappointment over the ethical breach.

words.definition: adjective: burdensome; difficult to bear
words.example: The task proved onerous, requiring a lot of effort. Despite the difficulty, completing it successfully brought immense satisfaction. I found the project's demands challenging, but the reward made the hard work worthwhile.

words.definition: noun: truthfulness and accuracy
words.example: Due to the high degree of truthfulness, the detective found it easy to find the criminal, because the witness gave veracity to the court.

words.definition: adjective: high‑sounding but with little meaning; inflated
words.example: The bombastic speaker used exaggerated language, making grand pronouncements that seemed designed more to impress the audience than to communicate actual information or substance.

words.definition: verb: to strip or rid of property or rights
words.example: I will divest my shares of the company because the business has had a rough year. Their profits went down, and I don't want to risk any more money on it.

words.definition: adjective: willing to obey rules or requests
words.example: The store's new policy made many customers compliant, but some still found ways to bend the rules.

words.definition: adjective: liable to change rapidly and unpredictably
words.example: The volatile nature of the market made investors nervous, as they worried about the possibility of sudden and unpredictable changes. It caused them to re-evaluate their investments.

words.definition: adjective: strongly supporting one side
words.example: The biased group's actions were viewed as partisan, favoring their own members over others. This led to intense disagreements, as some felt the decisions were unfair to those who didn't belong.

words.definition: adjective: implied though not directly stated
words.example: The subtle clues in her expression gave an implicit understanding of the situation, and everyone knew without needing an explanation or words, that something was not right, it was obvious to all.

words.definition: noun: conformity to accepted standards; correctness
words.example: She always behaved with propriety, never gossiping or causing any trouble, because she knew that her reputation was important for her career, and she wanted to be seen as professional.

words.definition: adjective: just coming into existence; beginning to develop
words.example: Because of the nascent technology, the company needed more time to fully develop its product to meet the demands of its consumers.

words.definition: verb: to disagree with authority
words.example: Amidst the heated debate, a wave of dissent surged, with many people openly disagreeing with the proposed changes, their voices echoing with disapproval and a determination to protect their beliefs.

words.definition: adjective: very weak or slight
words.example: The fragile bridge, its structure tenuous, swayed precariously in the wind, and the hikers worried about the integrity of its supports, as they were uncertain whether it would hold.

words.definition: verb: to become less intense or widespread
words.example: The rain began to abate as the storm moved eastward, allowing the sun to peek through the clouds and illuminate the colorful flowers in the garden, bringing joy

words.definition: noun: use of trickery to achieve a purpose
words.example: Due to the politician's chicanery, the public lost faith in the government. The lies and deception led many citizens to doubt the intentions and honesty of their leaders.

words.definition: adjective: not important or significant
words.example: The movie's plot was inconsequential to the overall themes, as the director focused on the visuals and atmosphere rather than a deep, meaningful story, and the audience was left confused.

words.definition: noun: craftiness
words.example: Little Timmy was full of guile, often telling his mommy someone was at the door--then, when her back was turned, he would raid the chocolate stash.

words.definition: noun: something that discourages action
words.example: The police presence served as a deterrent, making potential criminals reconsider their actions. They knew the risks of getting caught were high with officers nearby, discouraging any illegal behavior.

words.definition: adjective: cautious, not trusting
words.example: Years of being stuck in the loud and crowded shelter made the dog wary of other animals.

words.definition: noun: a speech praising someone who has died
words.example: The touching eulogy, filled with heartfelt memories and anecdotes, painted a vivid picture of the person's life, celebrating their kindness and the impact they had on others, leaving everyone deeply moved.

words.definition: noun: keen insight and quick judgment
words.example: Her business acumen was evident when she turned a small, struggling company into a profitable enterprise within just two years, demonstrating a keen understanding of the market and strategic decision-making.

words.definition: adjective: habitually reserved and uncommunicative
words.example: While the CEO enthusiastically shares his plans and agenda with all who will listen, the CFO is far more taciturn, rarely revealing his perspective.

words.definition: noun: an expert judge in matters of taste
words.example: The restaurant critic, a true connoisseur, savored the exquisite flavors of the dish. His discerning palate detected a hint of truffle, a whisper of citrus, and the perfect balance.

words.definition: adjective: intensely passionate
words.example: The ardent speeches from the politician were always filled with fervid language, captivating the audience with passionate calls to action, even though some felt the promises were exaggerated.

words.definition: adjective: careful to consider all circumstances; cautious
words.example: The detective, a circumspect individual, approached the crime scene cautiously, carefully examining every detail. His goal was to solve the case, understanding all clues.

words.definition: noun: a loud and continuous noise
words.example: The loud clamor of the crowd was almost unbearable, as everyone was screaming and shouting, hoping to get the attention of the performers who were on the stage.

words.definition: adjective: more than is needed; very fancy
words.example: Fido's birthday feast was lavish; most guests thought that a dog would not be able to appreciate the bits of gold in his steak-flavored ice cream.

words.definition: verb: to state or assert confidently
words.example: As he began to aver his point, the speaker realized that some audience members were losing interest. It became apparent that he needed to explain the situation, and the crowd began to listen.

words.definition: verb: to make easier
words.example: Classical music, unlike many types of music, will generally facilitate learning and improve memory.

words.definition: adjective: of the same or similar kind
words.example: The scientific study was homogeneous, with all participants sharing similar backgrounds, which unfortunately limited the diversity of perspectives and viewpoints within the research findings.

words.definition: adjective: able to express ideas clearly and effectively
words.example: He found it difficult to articulate his thoughts during the meeting because he was nervous, but he knew the importance of communicating effectively with his colleagues.

words.definition: noun: an eager willingness to do something
words.example: The first three weeks at his new job, Mark worked with such alacrity that upper management knew it would be giving him a promotion.

words.definition: noun: misconduct or wrongdoing (especially by a public official)
words.example: Not even the mayor’s trademark pearly-toothed grin could save him from charges of malfeasance: while in power, he’d been running an illegal gambling rink in the room behind his office.

words.definition: adjective: of broad scope; universal
words.example: Jonah’s friends said that Jonah’s taste in music was eclectic; Jonah was quick to point out that not only was his taste eclectic but it was also catholic: he enjoyed music from countries as far-flung as Mali and Mongolia.

words.definition: verb: to speak vaguely, usually with the intention to mislead or deceive
words.example: After Sharon brought the car home an hour after her curfew, she equivocated when her parents pointedly asked her where she had been.

words.definition: adjective: complete and wholly (usually modifying a noun with negative connotation)
words.example: An arrant fool, Lawrence surprised nobody when he lost all his money in a pyramid scheme that was every bit as transparent as it was corrupt.

words.definition: adjective: lecherous; sexually perverted
words.example: Lolita is a challenging novel for many, not necessarily because of the elevated prose style but because of the depravity of the main character, Humbert Humbert, who, as an old, lascivious man, lusts after a girl.

words.definition: noun: spirit of the times
words.example: Each decade has its own zeitgeist—the 1990’s was a prosperous time in which the promise of the American Dream never seemed more palpable.

words.definition: verb: to help pay the cost of, either in part or full
words.example: In order for Sean to attend the prestigious college, his generous uncle helped defray the excessive tuition with a monthly donation.

words.definition: adjective: produced by, or characterized by internal dissension
words.example: The controversial bill proved factious, as dissension even within parties resulted

words.definition: noun: a detested person; the source of somebody's hate
words.example: Hundreds of years ago, Galileo was anathema to the church; today the church is anathema to some on the left side of the political spectrum.

words.definition: noun: a person who has abandoned a religious faith or cause
words.example: An apostate of the Orthodox faith he was raised in, Sheldon continues to seek a more like-minded religious community.

words.definition: noun: an outcast
words.example: The once eminent scientist, upon being found guilty of faking his data, has become a pariah in the research community.

words.definition: adjective: without cunning or deceit
words.example: Despite the president's seemingly artless speeches, he was a skilled and ruthless negotiator.

words.definition: adjective: the lowest, without any moral principles
words.example: She was not so base as to begrudge the beggar the unwanted crumbs from her dinner plate.

words.definition: adjective: lazy and irresponsible
words.example: Two years after graduation, Charlie still lived with his parents and had no job, becoming more feckless with each passing day.

words.definition: noun: a person who thinks their country is always right and who is in favor of aggressive acts against other countries
words.example: In the days leading up to war, a nation typically breaks up into the two opposing camps: doves, who do their best to avoid war, and jingoists, who are only too eager to wave national flags from their vehicles and vehemently denounce those who do not do the same.

words.definition: adjective: haughty and disdainful; looking down on others
words.example: Nelly felt the Quiz Bowl director acted superciliously towards the underclassmen; really, she fumed, must he act so preternaturally omniscient each time he intones some obscure fact—as though everybody knows that Mt. Aconcagua is the highest peak in South America.

words.definition: noun: a strong verbal attack against a person or institution
words.example: Steve’s mom launched into a diatribe during the PTA meeting, contending that the school was little more than a daycare in which students stare at the wall and teachers stare at the chalkboard.

words.definition: verb: to intimidate
words.example: Do not be cowed by a 3,000-word vocabulary list: turn that list into a deck of flashcards!

words.definition: verb: to eliminate completely
words.example: When I turned 18, all of the shoplifting and jaywalking charges were expunged from my criminal record.

words.definition: noun: critical explanation or analysis, especially of a text
words.example: The Bible is fertile ground for exegesis—over the past five centuries there have been as many interpretations as there are pages in the Old Testament.

words.definition: adjective: intolerable, difficult to endure
words.example: Chester always tried to find some area in which he excelled above others; unsurprisingly, his co-workers found him insufferable and chose to exclude him from daily luncheons out.

words.definition: noun: the highest point
words.example: The apogee of the Viennese style of music, Mozart’s music continues to mesmerize audiences well into the 21st century.

words.definition: adjective: unfavorable; inconvenient
words.example: Some professors find teaching untoward as having to prepare for lectures and conduct office hours prevents them from focusing on their research.

words.definition: adjective: morose or gloomy
words.example: Deprived of sunlight, humans become saturnine; that’s why in very northerly territories people are encouraged to sit under an extremely powerful lamp, lest they become morose.

words.definition: verb: to make peace with
words.example: His opponents believed his gesture to be conciliatory, yet as soon as they put down their weapons, he unsheathed a hidden sword.

words.definition: adjective: intricate and complex
words.example: Getting a driver’s license is not simply a matter of taking a test; the regulations and procedures are so byzantine that many have found themselves at the mercy of the Department of Motor Vehicles.

words.definition: noun: the lowest point
words.example: For many pop music fans, the rap– and alternative-rock–dominated 90s were the nadir of musical expression.

words.definition: noun: change in one’s circumstances, usually for the worse
words.example: Even great rulers have their vicissitudes—massive kingdoms have diminished overnight, and once beloved kings have faced the scorn of angry masses.

words.definition: adjective: weighed-down; moving slowly
words.example: Laden with 20 kilograms of college text books, the freshman moved ponderously across the campus.

words.definition: adjective: prone to outbursts of temper; easily angered
words.example: While a brilliant lecturer, Mr. Dawson came across as choleric and unapproachable—very rarely did students come to his office hours.

words.definition: verb: to weaken (in terms of intensity); to taper off/become thinner.
words.example: Her animosity towards Bob attenuated over the years, and she even went so far as to invite him to her party.

words.definition: adjective: dull and lacking imagination
words.example: Unlike the talented artists in his workshop, Paul had no such bent for the visual medium, so when it was time for him to make a stained glass painting, he ended up with a prosaic mosaic.

words.definition: adjective: hasty or rash; verb: to cause to happen
words.example: Instead of conducting a thorough investigation after the city hall break-in, the governor acted precipitately, accusing his staff of aiding and abetting the criminals. / The government's mishandling of the hurricane's aftermath precipitated a widespread outbreak of looting and other criminal activity.

words.definition: adjective: done routinely and with little interest or care
words.example: The short film examines modern perfunctory cleaning rituals such as washing dishes, doing laundry and tooth-brushing.

words.definition: adjective: poor; having very little; noun: a poor or needy person
words.example: In the so-called Third World, many are indigent and only a privileged few have the resources to enjoy material luxuries. / The indigents, huddled under the overpass, tried to start a small bonfire in the hope of staying warm.

words.definition: verb: assume something is true (usu. followed by 'the question', meaning that you ask a question in which you assume something that hasn't been proven true)
words.example: By assuming that Charlie was headed to college—which he was not—Maggie begged the question when she asked him to which school he was headed in the Fall.

words.definition: adjective: arrogant; presumptuous
words.example: Mark was so convinced of his basketball skills that in his overweening pride he could not fathom that his name was not on the varsity list; he walked up to the basketball coach and told her she had forgotten to add his name.

words.definition: verb: to drink or absorb as if drinking
words.example: Plato imbibed Socrates’ teachings to such an extent that he was able to write volumes of work that he directly attributed, sometimes word for word, to Socrates.

words.definition: adjective: done diligently and carefully
words.example: An avid numismatist, Harold sedulously amassed a collection of coins from over 100 countries—an endeavor that took over fifteen years across five continents.

words.definition: adjective: having a fierce, savage nature
words.example: Standing in line for six hours, she became progressively truculent, yelling at DMV employees and elbowing other people waiting in line.

words.definition: adjective: likely to argue
words.example: Since old grandpa Harry became very contentious during the summer when only reruns were on T.V., the grandkids learned to hide from him at every opportunity.

words.definition: noun: depravity; a depraved act
words.example: During his reign, Caligula indulged in unspeakable sexual practices, so it is not surprising that he will forever be remembered for his turpitude.

words.definition: adjective: cautious, suspiciously reluctant to do something
words.example: Having received three speeding tickets in the last two months, Jack was chary of driving at all above the speed limit, even on a straight stretch of highway that looked empty for miles ahead.

words.definition: adjective: lacking manners or refinement
words.example: The manager was unnecessarily churlish to his subordinates, rarely deigning to say hello, but always quick with a sartorial jab if someone happened to be wearing anything even slightly mismatching.

words.definition: verb: to bow or act in a subservient manner
words.example: Paul kowtowed to his boss so often the boss herself became nauseated by his sycophancy.

words.definition: adjective: irritable and is likely to cause disruption
words.example: We rarely invite my fractious Uncle over for dinner; he always complains about the food, and usually launches into a tirade on some touchy subject.

words.definition: verb: to bully or intimidate
words.example: The boss’s hectoring manner put off many employees, some of whom quit as soon as they found new jobs.

words.definition: adjective: lacking money; poor; adjective: miserly
words.example: Truly penurious, Mary had nothing more than a jar full of pennies. / Warren Buffett, famous multi-billionaire, still drives a cheap sedan, not because he is penurious, but because luxury cars are gaudy and impractical.

words.definition: adjective: communicative, and prone to talking in a sociable manner
words.example: After a few sips of cognac, the octogenarian shed his irascible demeanor and became expansive, speaking fondly of the “good old days”.

words.definition: adjective: lacking money; poor
words.example: In extremely trying times, even the moderately wealthy, after a few turns of ill-fortune, can become impecunious.

words.definition: adjective: trifling or petty (a person)
words.example: English teachers are notorious for being picayune; however, the English language is so nuanced and sophisticated that often such teachers are not being contrary but are only adhering to the rules.

words.definition: adjective: to have a limited outlook or understanding
words.example: In gambling, the blinkered addict is easily influenced by past successes and/or past failures, forgetting that the outcome of any one game is independent of the games that preceded it.

words.definition: verb: to criticize harshly; to berate
words.example: Jason had dealt with disciplinarians before, but nothing prepared him for the first week of boot camp, as drill sergeants vituperated him for petty oversights such as forgetting to double knot the laces on his boots.

words.definition: verb: to manipulate voting districts in order to favor a particular political party
words.example: Years ago, savvy politicians had gerrymandered the city center to ensure their re-election.

words.definition: verb: to defraud or swindle
words.example: The so-called magical diet cure simply ended up mulcting Maria out of hundreds of dollars, but did nothing for her weight.

words.definition: verb: to remove objectionable material
words.example: The censor expurgated every reference to sex and drugs, converting the rapper's raunchy flow into a series of bleeps.

words.definition: adjective: to be overly theatrical
words.example: Though she received a B- on the test, she had such a histrionic outburst that one would have thought that she’d been handed a death sentence.

words.definition: noun: a confusing and potentially embarrassing situation
words.example: The chef cook-off featured one gourmand who had the unfortunate distinction of mixing the wrong broths, creating an imbroglio that diners would not soon forget.

words.definition: noun: a grouchy, surly person
words.example: Since Uncle Mike was the family curmudgeon, each Thanksgiving he was plied with copious amounts of wine, in the hope that he would become less grouchy.

words.definition: adjective: easily excused or forgiven; pardonable
words.example: His traffic violations ran the gamut from the venial to the egregious—on one occasion he simply did not come to a complete stop; another time he tried to escape across state lines at speeds in excess of 140 mph.

words.definition: adjective: artificial; not natural
words.example: The defendant’s story was largely factitious and did not accord with eyewitness testimonies.

words.definition: adjective: to be biased against due to envy or prejudice
words.example: Shelly was jaundiced towards Olivia; though the two had once been best friends, Olivia had become class president, prom queen, and, to make matters worse, the girlfriend of the one boy Shelly liked.

words.definition: noun: the confusion of a word with another word that sounds similar
words.example: Whenever I looked glum, my mother would offer to share 'an amusing antidote' with me—an endearing malapropism of 'anecdote' that never failed to cheer me up.

words.definition: verb: to make objections while pleading
words.example: The mothers of the kidnapped victims remonstrated to the rogue government to release their children, claiming that the detention violated human rights.

words.definition: noun: a person who indulges in luxury
words.example: Despite the fact that he’d maxed out fifteen credit cards, Max was still a sybarite at heart: when the police found him, he was at a $1,000 an hour spa in Manhattan, getting a facial treatment.

words.definition: adjective: irritable; always angry
words.example: Rex was bilious all morning, and his face would only take on a look of contentedness when he’d had his morning cup of coffee.

words.definition: adjective: illusive; unreal
words.example: Those suffering from malaria fall into a feverish sleep, their world a whirligig of phantasmagoria; if they recover, they are unsure of what actually took place and what was simply a product of their febrile imaginations.

words.definition: noun: calmness or poise in difficult situations
words.example: The hostage negotiator exhibited a sangfroid that oftentimes was more menacing than the sword at his throat, or the gun at his head.

words.definition: adjective: having clarity in terms of expression
words.example: Her limpid prose made even the most recondite subjects accessible to all.

words.definition: verb: to placate or appease
words.example: The two sons, plying their angry father with cheesy neckties for Christmas, were hardly able to propitiate him – the father already had a drawer full of ones he had never worn before or ever planned to.

words.definition: adjective: overly emotional and sad
words.example: Just as those who were alive during the 70’s are mortified that they once cavorted about in bellbottoms, many who lived during the 80’s are now aghast at the maudlin pop songs they used to enjoy—really, just what exactly is a total eclipse of the heart?

words.definition: noun: abusive or denunciatory language
words.example: The Internet has unleashed the invectives in many of us; many people post stinging criticism on the comments section underneath newspaper articles or YouTube videos.

words.definition: adjective: dull; lacking flavor; adjective: immature; childish
words.example: Although many top chefs have secured culinary foam's popularity in haute cuisine, Waters criticizes it for being jejune and unfilling. / Her boss further cemented his reputation for being jejune after throwing a fit when the water cooler wasn't refilled.

words.definition: adjective: likely to lean towards a controversial view
words.example: Because political mudslinging has become a staple of the 24-hour media cycle, most of us, despite protestations to the contrary, are tendentious on many of today’s pressing issues.

words.definition: adjective: terribly evil
words.example: For fans of the Harry Potter series, the fell Lord Voldemort, who terrorized poor Harry for seven lengthy installments, has finally been vanquished by the forces of good—unless, that is, JK Rowling decides to come out of retirement.

words.definition: noun: a person who has recently reached a position of power; a social climber
words.example: The city center was aflutter with arrivistes who tried to outdo one another with their ostentatious sports cars and chic evening dress.

words.definition: verb: to curse and hiss at
words.example: Though the new sitcom did decently in the ratings, the critic execrated the show, saying that it was nothing more than a terrible pastiche of tired clichés and canned laughter.

words.definition: noun: greed for money
words.example: Some people believe that amassing as much wealth as possible is the meaning to life—yet they often realize that cupidity brings anything but happiness.

words.definition: adjective: to be moralizing, usually in a pompous sense
words.example: The old man, casting his nose up in the air at the group of adolescents, intoned sententiously, 'Youth is wasted on the young.'

words.definition: verb: to limit or qualify a statement; to avoid making a direct statement
words.example: When asked why he had decided to buy millions of shares at the very moment the tech company's stock soared, the CEO hedged, mentioning something vague about gut instinct.

words.definition: noun: a person who has suddenly become wealthy, but not socially accepted as part of a higher class
words.example: The theater was full of parvenus who each thought that they were surrounded by true aristocrats.

words.definition: adjective: bossy and domineering
words.example: My sister used to peremptorily tell me to do the dishes, a chore I would either do perfunctorily or avoid doing altogether.

words.definition: noun: a strict disciplinarian
words.example: The job seemed perfect to Rebecca, until she found out that her boss was a total martinet; after each project the boss would come by to scrutinize—and inevitably criticize—every little detail of the work Rebecca had done.

words.definition: adjective: to be deliberately teasing
words.example: The baroness was arch, making playful asides to the townspeople; yet because they couldn't pick up on her dry humor, they thought her supercilious.

words.definition: noun: exaltation to divine status; the highest point of development
words.example: As difficult as it is to imagine, the apotheosis of Mark Zuckerberg’s career, many believe, is yet to come.

words.definition: noun: something that has been changed numerous times but on which traces of former iterations can still be seen
words.example: The downtown was a palimpsest of the city’s checkered past: a new Starbucks had opened up next to an abandoned, shuttered building, and a freshly asphalted road was inches away from a pothole large enough to swallow a small dog.

words.definition: adjective: fallen into a state of ignorance
words.example: Far from being a period of utter benightedness, The Medieval Ages produced some great works of theological speculation.

words.definition: adjective: readily taking on different roles; versatile
words.example: Peter Sellers was truly a protean actor—in Doctor Strangelove he played three very different roles: a jingoist general, a sedate President and a deranged scientist.

words.definition: verb: to criticize very harshly
words.example: Entrusted with the prototype to his company’s latest smartphone, Larry, during a late night karaoke bout, let the prototype slip into the hands of a rival company—the next day Larry was excoriated, and then fired.

words.definition: adjective: describing a victory that comes at such a great cost that the victory is not worthwhile
words.example: George W. Bush’s win in the 2000 election was in many ways a pyrrhic victory: the circumstances of his win alienated half of the U.S. population.

words.definition: adjective: extremely optimistic
words.example: Even in the midst of a lousy sales quarter, Debbie remained Pollyannaish, never losing her shrill voice and wide smile, even when prospective customers hung up on her.

words.definition: adjective: related to fashion or clothes
words.example: Monte was astute at navigating the world of finance; sartorially, however, he was found wanting—he typically would attempt to complement his beige tie with a gray suit and white pants.

words.definition: adjective: smooth and sweet-sounding
words.example: Chelsea’s grandmother thought Franz Schubert’s music to be the most mellifluous ever written; Chelsea demurred, and to her grandmother’s chagrin, would blast Rihanna on the home stereo speakers.

words.definition: adjective: filled with courage or valor
words.example: For its raid on the Bin Laden’s compound in Abbottabad, Seal Team Six has become, for many Americans, the embodiment of mettle.

words.definition: noun: a traitor
words.example: History looks unfavorably upon quislings; indeed they are accorded about the same fondness as Nero—who watched his city burn down while playing the violin.

words.definition: adjective: wildly idealistic; impractical
words.example: For every thousand startups with quixotic plans to be the next big name in e-commerce, only a handful ever become profitable.

words.definition: verb: to persuade somebody that his/her belief is not valid
words.example: As a child, I was quickly disabused of the notion that Santa Claus was a rotund benefactor of infinite largess—one night I saw my mother diligently wrapping presents and storing them under our Christmas tree.

words.definition: noun: joy from watching the suffering of others
words.example: From his warm apartment window, Stanley reveled in schadenfreude as he laughed at the figures below, huddled together in the arctic chill.

words.definition: noun: a force that cannot be stopped
words.example: Napoleon was considered a juggernaut until he decided to invade Russia in winter; after which, his once indomitable army was decimated by cold and famine.
